Property & Real Estate Law

Property Registration & Land Mutation (Khatauni) Rules: Preventing Real Estate Fraud

✍️ Advocate RK & Associates📅 2026-08-18⏱️ 6 min read

Registration vs Mutation: Understanding the Difference

When purchasing immovable property in India, two distinct legal processes take place: 1. Property Registration (Sale Deed): Transfer of title executed between buyer and seller and registered before the Sub-Registrar Office under the Registration Act, 1908. 2. Mutation of Title (Khatauni / Revenue Records): Updating official government revenue records by replacing the previous owner's name with the new purchaser's name.

Pre-Purchase Real Estate Due Diligence Checklist

#

1. 30-Year Title Search Verification

Verify the historical chain of title deeds for at least the past 30 years to confirm that the vendor possesses absolute, unencumbered ownership rights.

#

2. Encumbrance Certificate (EC)

Obtain an Encumbrance Certificate from the Sub-Registrar Office to ensure the property is free from pending bank mortgages, litigation, or monetary liabilities.

#

3. Revenue Record Verification (Khatauni & Bhu-Naksha)

Cross-examine the Khatauni extract, Khasra numbers, land area, and zoning categories (agricultural vs non-agricultural) with revenue department records.

#

4. Verification of Pending Family & Court Disputes

Ensure that the land is not subject to family partition suits, ceiling laws, or court injunction orders.

The Land Mutation (Dakhl-Kharij) Procedure

After executing the sale deed, file an application for mutation before the Tehsildar Court. Following public notice and revenue field inspection by the Patwari/Lekhpal, the purchaser's name is updated in the official Khatauni records.

📌 Key Legal Takeaways

  • Registration transfers contractual title; mutation updates government revenue records.
  • A 30-year chain deed search ensures undisputed historical ownership.
  • Encumbrance Certificates verify freedom from mortgages and statutory charges.
  • In case of land disputes, temporary stay applications (Order 39 CPC) can be filed in Civil Court.

❓ Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

Does property registration automatically update revenue records?

While some urban areas have integrated digital reporting, filing a formal mutation application before the Tehsildar Court remains essential for agricultural and revenue lands.

What legal remedy exists if someone illegally encroaches on registered land?

A civil suit for permanent injunction along with an urgent application for temporary injunction (Order 39 CPC) can be instituted in the Civil Court.
